questions.q: In ImageCompositeMasked, what does a mask value of 1 at a pixel give?
options: The destination pixel
The average of source and destination
The source pixel
Black
questions.why: The node computes mask · source + (1 − mask) · destination. In every ComfyUI inpainting node a mask value of 1 means new content.

questions.q: A flat 0.8 image is composited over a flat 0.2 image. What is the largest step between neighbouring output pixels with a hard mask edge, and with an 8-pixel FeatherMask ramp?
options: 0.600 and 0.075, because the step is 0.6 divided by the ramp width
0.600 and 0.600, because a feather only changes the colour
0.075 and 0.600, because a hard edge is smoother
0.800 and 0.100, because the step is the new value divided by the width
questions.answer: 0.600 and 0.075, because the step is 0.6 divided by the ramp width
questions.why: Neighbouring outputs differ by |new − old| times the difference of their mask values: 0.6 for a hard edge and 0.6 / 8 = 0.075 for a ramp that rises by 1/8 per pixel.

questions.q: What does the FeatherMask node do?
options: It blurs the edge of any shape inside the mask
It grows the mask by a few pixels
It thresholds the mask to 0 and 1
It multiplies the columns and rows next to the borders of the mask image by a linear ramp
questions.answer: It multiplies the columns and rows next to the borders of the mask image by a linear ramp
questions.why: The ramp runs (x + 1) / n over the n pixels at each border. To soften an edge inside the image, blur the mask (ImageBlur through MaskToImage and ImageToMask), and note that VAEEncodeForInpaint rounds the mask again.

questions.q: A hard pixel mask starts at column 21 and goes to an 8x latent. What mask does the sampler effectively see in the lab?
options: A half-strength cell at column 21
The same edge at column 24: cells 0 0 0 1 1 1 1 1
An edge at column 16
A smooth ramp across all 8 cells
questions.answer: The same edge at column 24: cells 0 0 0 1 1 1 1 1
questions.why: Bilinear interpolation without antialiasing reads only pixels 3 and 4 of each 8-pixel cell. Pixels 19 and 20 are both 0, so cell 2 is 0 and the edge lands on the cell boundary at 24.

questions.q: Why can a mask stripe 3 pixels wide be invisible to the sampler, and what does grow_mask_by do about it?
options: The sampler ignores any mask thinner than 8 pixels, and growing turns the sampler off
The stripe is blurred away by the VAE, and growing sharpens it
The downscale reads only two pixels per axis per latent cell, which the stripe can miss. Growing widens it to 8 pixels so it never vanishes
The mask is rounded to 0, and growing rounds it to 1
questions.answer: The downscale reads only two pixels per axis per latent cell, which the stripe can miss. Growing widens it to 8 pixels so it never vanishes
questions.why: In the lab the stripe has largest latent value 0.00 at 4 of 8 offsets. After grow_mask_by 6, a 3-pixel stripe becomes 8 pixels wide and the smallest value over the offsets is 0.50.

questions.q: In the lab's sampler bookkeeping with a stand-in model, what is the final latent where the mask is 0, and where it is 0.5?
options: The model's output in both places
The original latent where 0, and the model's output where 0.5
Noise where 0, and the original where 0.5
The original latent where 0, and half the model's last output plus half the original where 0.5
questions.answer: The original latent where 0, and half the model's last output plus half the original where 0.5
questions.why: KSamplerX0Inpaint replaces the prediction with m · D + (1 − m) · L at every step, and the last step lands on it. The lab's largest differences from those expressions are 0.0.
